## Pre-fetched Issue Comments

**SilvioBaratto** (2026-06-11T18:48:03Z):
> Missing deck shuffle in the setup flow. The reference implementation (`src/env.py:186`) calls `s.rng.shuffle(s.deck)` at the very start of `_setup_board`, before territory distribution. None of the six acceptance-criteria functions in this issue mention shuffling the deck, so as specified `new_state` always returns cards in the fixed order `[0, 1, …, 43]`. Every game regardless of seed would draw cards in the same sequence, breaking the research goal of seed-reproducible diversity.
> 
> Fix: add `state.rng.shuffle(state.deck)` inside `distribute_territories` (first line, before the territory-order shuffle) or add a dedicated `shuffle_deck(state)` helper called by the board-setup orchestrator, and add a determinism assertion in `tests/test_board.py` that verifies two `new_state(3, 42)` + `distribute_territories` calls produce identical deck orders.

**SilvioBaratto** (2026-06-15T13:44:21Z):
> Missing deck-shuffle step — the six acceptance functions never shuffle `state.deck`, but the reference setup (`src/env.py:186`) calls `state.rng.shuffle(state.deck)` at the very start of board setup, before territory distribution. As specified, `new_state` leaves the deck as the fixed sequence `list(range(44))` = `[0,1,...,43]`, so card draws come out in identical order in every game regardless of seed — eliminating per-seed card diversity that the research goal depends on.
> 
> Fix: add an explicit acceptance criterion that the deck is shuffled via `state.rng` during setup — either as the first line of `distribute_territories(state)` (`state.rng.shuffle(state.deck)`, before the territory-order shuffle) or as a dedicated `shuffle_deck(state)` helper. Add a determinism test in `tests/test_board.py` asserting two `new_state(3, 42)` + setup calls produce identical deck orders, AND a test asserting the post-setup deck is not the unshuffled `list(range(44))`.

## Pre-fetched Issue Comments

**SilvioBaratto** (2026-06-11T18:48:05Z):
> Naming inconsistency with issue #49: this issue says "Use `CardManager.draw_card` and `CardManager.transfer_cards` from `src/env_core/cards.py`", but issue #49 specifies stateless **module-level functions** (`draw_card`, `transfer_cards`) — no `CardManager` class. An implementer following both issues literally will either create an undocumented class in `cards.py` (violating #49's design) or fail to call the functions correctly.
> 
> Fix: replace both references with the module-level call form: `cards.draw_card(state, player)` and `cards.transfer_cards(state, from_player, to_player)` (where `cards` is the imported `src.env_core.cards` module).

**SilvioBaratto** (2026-06-15T13:44:22Z):
> Card-module interface mismatch. This issue's context says "Use `CardManager.draw_card` and `CardManager.transfer_cards` from `src/env_core/cards.py`", implying a `CardManager` class. The card module is specified and built as stateless module-level functions (`draw_card(state, player)`, `transfer_cards(state, from_player, to_player)`), so `CardManager.draw_card` will not resolve and combat will fail to import.
> 
> Fix: change the context and implementation notes to call the module-level functions directly — e.g. `from src.env_core.cards import draw_card, transfer_cards` then `draw_card(state, current_player)` / `transfer_cards(state, defender_player, current_player)`. No class accessor exists; align the combat acceptance criteria (card draw on capture, card transfer on elimination) to the module-level API.
> 
> Note on the capture-move bounds (`last_capture_dice <= move <= armies[last_attacker]-1`): verified sound — a capturing roll requires winning every compared pair against the defender's remaining armies, so the attacker loses zero armies on the capturing roll and `armies[attacker]-1 >= dice` always holds. No empty-range deadlock. Keep the bounds as specified.
